chunks: Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah who said, 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying to a man,'

'Why is it that you hurt the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' So the man said to him, 'May I be your ransom! How do we hurt him?' He said, 'Do you not know that your actions are presented to him? So when he sees that they contain [acts of] disobedience to Allah, that hurts him. Do not hurt the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and please him [instead (by your good deeds)].'
ai.seo_question: How do the deeds of believers affect the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* elucidates the concept of *Ta'arud al-A'mal* (the presentation of deeds), where the Prophet’s spiritual state is directly affected by the moral conduct of his Ummah. It underscores the Shia emphasis on the Prophet’s living, responsive connection to believers, transforming personal piety into an act of honoring the Prophet himself. Consequently, avoiding sin is not merely a legal obligation but a means of bringing joy (*Surur*) to the Prophet, reinforcing the intercessory and emotional bond between the Imamate and the faithful.
